title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows and optimize cache/parallelism
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Split CI workflows to improve cache hit rates and reduce pipeline duration. No user-facing changes. Rollout covers only CI infra and release automation.
description: Motivation: our monolithic CI workflow grew slow and brittle. Lint, tests, and release steps were coupled which makes cache keys collide and increases feedback loop time for PRs. This PR splits lint/test/release into separate workflows, consolidates cache keys into a central script, improves job matrix parallelism, and bumps a handful of GitHub actions to their maintained versions. Summary of changes: split .github/workflows/ci.yml into three workflows (.github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml); introduce .github/scripts/cache-key.sh to compute stable cache keys based on lockfiles and action versions; standardize Node in JS/TS jobs to node:20 and add node-version matrix for long-term reproducibility; reduce redundant install steps by promoting a shared restore-deps step; tune parallelism for unit/integration tests to 8 parallel runners based on historical flakiness and infra capacity. Checklist: - [x] split workflows and wire provenance/labels - [x] validate cache key determinism locally and in CI - [x] run full repo test matrix on a cohort of active feature branches - [x] add fallbacks so release workflow requires manual approval for protected branches - [x] document changes in dev-infra/README. Impact and rollout: low-risk infra-only change. Merged behind a small canary where top 50 active PRs were opted in for two business days. Any failures roll back via revert PR. Followups: instrument workflow timings and cache hit-rate in Grafana (ENG-9340), and roll out similar cache-key strategy to the redwood-sdk-* repositories.

review_comments: Jordan Lee: Nice split, can you explain the cache-key.sh format and how it avoids invalidation when only docs change?

Ava Martinez: cache-key.sh hashes package-lock.json plus a pinned-actions.txt file. Docs-only changes are excluded by ignoring certain paths and by using the lockfile as the primary dependency fingerprint.
Priya Patel: Tests look good but we saw a flaky integration test in the first run. Suggest reducing concurrency on that job and adding a retry on the specific step.
Ava Martinez: lowered concurrency for integration-suite to 4 and added a single-step retry for the db-setup step. Reran and the job stabilized.
Samir Gupta: Approving after verifying release workflow requires ENV_PROTECT approval and that artifacts are uploaded correctly.
ci_checks: ubuntu-22.04:test matrix (flaky first run -> re-run passed)
notes: This PR focuses on repo hygiene and CI performance. No product behavior changes. Observability follow-up assigned to ENG-9340.
migration_steps: None for application code. Devs should update local CI docs if they rely on the old single ci.yml. CLI dev scripts that triggered the monolithic workflow have been updated to use the workflow_dispatch triggers where appropriate.
